source.archive: Cui, Li, and Zhou OSF replication archive
authorized_normalizations: Deleted the stray airport-security lead-in from dermatologist arms.
Standardized item order across contexts without changing item meaning.

design.primary_estimand: mean high-functional-intimacy minus low-functional-intimacy, averaged across airport and dermatology contexts

population.simulation_target: Adult imagining a routine airport-security or dermatology encounter

materials.participant_role: Act as the person receiving the professional service. Respond for yourself and do not analyze the experiment.
materials.common_scenario: Imagine the routine professional encounter described below.

airport_high.label: Airport High
airport_high.stimulus: At airport security, an officer conducts a hands-on pat-down of your body.

airport_low.label: Airport Low
airport_low.stimulus: At airport security, an officer searches your carry-on bag without touching your body.

dermatology_high.label: Dermatology High
dermatology_high.stimulus: At a dermatology visit, the dermatologist conducts a full-body skin examination.

dermatology_low.label: Dermatology Low
dermatology_low.stimulus: At a dermatology visit, the dermatologist examines a mole on your hand.

materials.response_instruction: Rate every item from 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree) and return only integer item responses.

items.text: I would prefer not to smile at the professional.
I would prefer not to ask the professional's name.
I would prefer to avoid eye contact with the professional.
I would prefer not to self-disclose to the professional.
The professional would be physically close to me.
The professional would enter my personal space.
The interaction would involve personal contact.

research_restricted.aligned_hypothesis_text: High functional intimacy increases preferred social distance after averaging across contexts.
research_restricted.reversed_hypothesis_text: High functional intimacy does not increase preferred social distance after averaging across contexts.
